correctness.rationale: Step 1 follows because both original and transformed n-th powers are the positive period product times the n-step shift (whose spectral radius is one). Weighted AM–GM proves the lower bound. The coordinatewise second derivative of the cyclic log-product is strictly positive for 0<λ<1, so every maximizer over a log-weight cube lies at an extreme vertex. At each binary vertex the product is exactly Θ^k, where k is the number of up-down transition pairs, with k≤floor(n/2); maximally alternating patterns realize equality and give the complete equality classification, including odd n. The λ optimum is uniquely 1/2. Exact-rational verifier independently checks finite cases, but the universal result relies on the analytical proof. No nonstandard unproved lemma is used.
